steps.text: Stir flour and 1 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Mix water, yeast, and sugar in a large bowl. Let stand until yeast begins to form a creamy foam, about 5 minutes.

Stir half the flour mixture into yeast mixture until no dry spots remain. Stir in remaining flour, 1/2 cup at a time, mixing well after each addition. When dough pulls together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.

Lightly oil a large bowl, then place dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a light cloth and let rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) until doubled in volume, about 1 hour. Punch dough down, divide into 4 equal pieces, and form each into a ball.
Preheat oven with a pizza stone to 500 degrees F (260 degrees C).

Stretch out and pat 1 dough ball to form a circle 10 to 12 inches in diameter. Place dough on a lightly floured pizza peel. Top with 1/2 cup of tomato sauce and spread to cover within an inch of the edge of the dough. Arrange 5 slices of mozzarella cheese on top of the tomato sauce, then place 5 basil leaves on top. Drizzle pizza with 1 tablespoon olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt to taste. Repeat for 3 remaining dough balls.
Slide each pizza onto the pizza stone in the preheated oven. Bake until cheese is bubbly and the underside of the crust is golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Authentic Pizza Margherita
raw_recipe.description: Inspired by the pizza at Bar Del Corso, this Pizza Margherita features tomato sauce, mozzarella, and basil, with just a hint of sea salt.

video.description: In this video, Jerry Corso, owner of Bar del Corso, reveals the secret to making the best pizza. You’ll see how to make a simple margherita pizza using just a handful of ingredients, including fresh basil and mozzarella. The key is to start with fresh, quality ingredients and then allow the ingredients to really show themselves off. You’ll also learn the benefits of cooking your pizza on a pizza stone on high heat. Find out what makes a really good pizza. It may be less than you think.

review.reviewBody: Very quick, easy and came out great. I preheated my oven a bit before placing the bowl of dough in it and it doubled in about 20 minutes.

I used my own dough recipe which is way better than this one. To 1 cup of warm water add 2 1/4 tsps of yeast and 2 tsp of olive oil. Add 2.5 cups of flour to the yeast mixture in Kitchen Aid mixer. Mix until a ball is created. Place in an oiled bowl, cover and let rise for 1-2 hours. Perfect dough everytime.

I have now made this recipe many times. It IS great and just like a Margherita pizza should be. I made only a few changes. First off I only use 3 cups of flour, anymore makes it dry and unmanageable. I use quick rise yeast too. I also use my food processor to do the dough which works great. I divide mine in HALF. I found them to be too small if divided into 4. I also just use a pizza pan and not oven tiles. I just keep an eye on it but it takes about the same time to bake. I also put a few more Basil leaves on because the shrink when baked. So I put on at least 8. The mozzarella even in large slices should melt down and spread out but if that doesn't work for you tear it into smaller pieces and dot it all over. Just do not use too much or it can make the pizza too WET.

This recipe is totally wrong. If you are going to use that much flour you have to add another cup of water. 
To bake at 500 degrees you get top and bottom crust and RAW inside. Reduce heat to 450. Bake for 16 minutes.

I substitute 1/4 cup cornmeal for flour. I've also found that whole milk mozzarella is easier to handle in a semi-frozen state and I cube it instead of just slice it. 

My "pizza sauce" is little more than a can of drained plum tomatoes which I puree with an immersion blender and add a little bit of olive oil, black pepper, a pinch of sugar and a pinch of sea salt. Simple.

This makes a delicious pizza. It takes some time and effort but well worth it. I followed as directed and had excellent results. My first time baking a pizza on a stone, will not make one any other way now. I made only 1 pizza, wrapped remaining 3 balls with plastic wrap and put in fridge. Next day removed one, let come to room temp and punched back down. Made pizza, came out as perfect as the first. The whole family loved this pizza. Thank you for the recipe.

Very easy good base recipe on its own! After a few times I added 2 TBLS of wine, 1/2 TBLS of basil, 1/2 TSP onion powder. With those alterations I had several people compliment MY Sauce itself rather than just, this is good pizza!

Delicious and fresh! I did not use pizza sauce, instead I used sliced homegrown tomatoes that I lightly salted and let drain in a strainer to get the excess liquid out. The dough was super easy to make and I used whole wheat flour to replace a cup of AP flour. So simple.

I have to agree with the majority that this pizza is out of this world! My kids thought it was better than our favorite pizza joint. I used Contadina Pizza Sauce (all there products are fabulous in my opinion), peppers, onions, pepperoni, and spinach. I tried both the shredded mozzarella and the fresh mozzarella to see the difference and hands down the fresh mozzarella was much, much more tasty. I did not have sea salt and like spinach on my pizza, so I did not use basil. I topped it off with olive oil and cracked black pepper. As a well-known picky eater, I can't say enough about how good this pizza is. I would recommend trying a second time if you did not rate it well the first time. DELICIOUS!!!!!!

I really liked this base recipe but found the dough over- floured. I would reduce the flour by a good 1/2c next time. Otherwise, I used a white sauce instead of red so not technically a margherita but was absolutely wonderful and easy to make thin slightly chewy crust with. Delish!

Easy recipe. Fast to make. No rise time required for the dough. Used Fleishman's Yeast for PIZZA dough. No proofing needed. Crust turned out very nice. This pizza was good, but I still prefer a brick oven pizza.
Fabulous 20 minute prep to homemade pizza! Kids devour this. I substituted spinach leaves for the fresh basil and it was just as good!

I made this in a 12" cast iron fry pan using the pizza dough recipe that came with my food processor. While I did use the steps in this recipe, I made so many changes to the ingredients that I can't really give a fair review to the recipe. The end result, however, was the best pizza I have ever made. I did use a good quality 12 oz. Jar of pizza sauce to which I added oregano, garlic, and basil, instead of the 24 oz. Jar of marinara. My base was 1/4 pound each of Hamburg and mild Italian sausage, sauteed with 1/2 cup chopped onion and 1/2 tsp. Garlic salt and 1/2 tsp each oregano and basil. Half the cheeses were added to the crust first, then the Hamburg mixture, then the sauce, then the rest of the cheese on top. I sprinkled the cheese lightly with oregano and basil, then sprayed the top lightly with olive oil. Baked on lower rack in my electric oven at 500° for about 17 minutes. My picky husband loved it, too. Hopefully, I'll remember how I made it so I can make it again.😯

this was fairly good! I don't own a pizza stone so I just used a cookie sheet and the crust came out a bit floury and pasty, I'm not sure if it was a problem with the lack of pizza stone or the yeast I used that caused that. I added some garlic and oregano to the sauce because that's how I like it, overall tasted good!
I didn’t use the dough recipe, but I did use the method for the toppings and it came out great! Best pizza I ever made! Will be making this over and over again as long as I continue to LOVE pizza!
This is my go to pizza dough recipe! My family really enjoys the pizza a lot! I also prefer a homemade pizza sauce which makes it that much more delicious.

This dough is a pain to make. It's dry and works hard. I had to add in extra water to make it work at all. To make it work even better, it probably needed oil of some sort. However, the end result was a perfect crispy/soft crust. So I guess the work is worth the end result. The rest of the recipe is solid and made one of the best margherita pizzas that we've ever had.
I love this pizza, and it always works out well.
Did it! Easy to make, easy to understand And it was delicious!
